# Dot-com bubble

The NASDAQ Composite index peaked at 5,048.62 on 10 March 2000. Between 1995 and its peak in March 2000, the NASDAQ Composite rose by 600%. At its trough on 9 October 2002 the NASDAQ-100 had fallen to 1,114, down 78% from its peak. By the end of the 2002 stock market downturn, stocks had lost $5 trillion in market capitalisation since the peak. By November 2000 most internet stocks had declined 75% from their highs, wiping out $1.755 trillion in value.

The late-1990s internet boom inflated on investment far ahead of profit, and when it burst the speculation died but the technology did not.
Investment poured into internet startups, often before they had profits, or even a viable business. When reality caught up in 2000, tech stocks collapsed. The technology endured.
